items.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant Interview, 1962-05-17
items.q: The interviewee corrects the interviewer's identification of the singer, stating 'He's the one that sings all the Creole songs,' indicating recognition but no personal interaction described.

ctx.x: Oh, they're keeping it up. Very good. I often ask him what he would do in his band when he'd be gone. He says, well, I tried to teach the youngsters, but they won't listen. I say, but please leave somebody in your place. Just don't pass on and don't, you know, don't leave that to someone. So, but Eddie French. Albert French. Albert French. He really, and the one who sings on the mic. I don't know his name, but he sings all the Creole favorites.
All the Creole. All the. Brother Cornbread. His name is Joseph Thomas, but they call him.

Thomas. That's right. Albert Thomas. Yeah, yeah. George Thomas. George Thomas. George Thomas. He's the one that sings all the Creole songs. Yeah. He's old. And so they have a beautiful, wonderful band. Oh. And they played all the old pieces. This is funny.
